beats.title: Aibak Begins the Qutb Minar
beats.description: A Delhi commander started a towering red sandstone minaret beside the new mosque to proclaim the arrival of Muslim rule.
beats.note: Sources give 1192 to 1202; 1199 is the most widely cited start.

beats.title: Aibak Founds the Delhi Sultanate
beats.description: After his master was assassinated, a former slave general took power in northern India and began a line of Delhi sultans.

beats.title: Caliph Recognises Iltutmish
beats.description: A robe of honour and a formal letter from Baghdad confirmed a Delhi sultan as a legitimate Muslim ruler of Hindustan.

beats.title: Jalaluddin Khalji Seizes the Throne
beats.description: An aging Turkic noble overthrew the last of the slave-dynasty rulers, ending the first sultan line and starting a new one.

beats.title: Alauddin Khalji Murders His Uncle
beats.description: After a successful raid on a Deccan kingdom, an ambitious governor killed the sultan who trusted him and took Delhi's crown.

beats.title: Alauddin Captures Chittor
beats.description: A Delhi sultan besieged and took the great Rajput hill fortress, an event later wrapped in legend and epic poetry.

beats.title: Tughluq Moves Capital to Daulatabad
beats.description: A sultan ordered Delhi's people to march hundreds of miles south to a new capital, a plan he later abandoned.

beats.title: Tughluq Issues Token Currency
beats.description: A sultan short of silver ordered brass and copper coins to be accepted at silver's value, and forgers soon flooded the market.

beats.title: Firoz Shah Founds Firozabad
beats.description: A sultan built a new walled city on the Yamuna beside Delhi, crowned by a palace with an Ashokan pillar on its roof.
beats.why_in: founding by Sultan Firoz Shah Tughlaq

beats.title: Timur Sacks Delhi
beats.description: A Central Asian conqueror routed the sultan's army and plundered the capital, leaving the sultanate shattered for decades.

beats.title: Khizr Khan Founds Sayyid Dynasty
beats.description: A governor installed by the Central Asian invader took Delhi and began a short-lived line of sultans.

beats.title: Bahlul Lodi Founds the Lodi Dynasty
beats.description: An Afghan chieftain took the throne at Delhi, beginning the last ruling line of the old sultanate.

beats.title: Sikandar Lodi Founds Agra
beats.description: A Delhi sultan moved his base to a Yamuna riverside site and laid out the city that later became a Mughal capital.

beats.title: Babur Wins at Panipat
beats.description: A Timurid prince with cannon and matchlocks defeated the Delhi sultan's far larger army and opened the way to a new empire.

beats.title: Babur Defeats the Rajputs at Khanwa
beats.description: The first Mughal emperor routed a Rajput confederation led by a famed Mewar king, securing his hold on northern India.

beats.title: Sher Shah Routs Humayun at Kannauj
beats.description: An Afghan commander beat the Mughal emperor on the Ganges and drove him into exile, taking the Delhi throne himself.
beats.why_in: Humayun's defeat; Sher Shah rules Delhi

beats.title: Humayun Recovers Delhi
beats.description: After years in Persian exile, the dethroned Mughal emperor defeated the Sur rulers and returned to his capital.

beats.title: Akbar Is Crowned
beats.description: A boy of thirteen was enthroned as Mughal emperor on a battlefield in the Punjab, and went on to rule for nearly half a century.

beats.title: Akbar Abolishes the Jizya
beats.description: The emperor ended the special tax on non-Muslims, a step toward his policy of tolerance across his many subjects.

beats.title: Humayun's Tomb Is Begun
beats.description: A widow of the second Mughal emperor oversaw a garden tomb in red sandstone and marble, a forerunner of the Taj Mahal.

beats.title: Akbar Founds Fatehpur Sikri
beats.description: The emperor began a new red sandstone capital near a Sufi saint's home, then abandoned it little more than a decade later.

beats.title: Mughals Fight at Haldighati
beats.description: Akbar's army, led by a Rajput general, met the Mewar ruler Maharana Pratap in a narrow mountain pass in Rajasthan.

beats.title: Akbar Proclaims Din-i Ilahi
beats.description: The emperor announced a syncretic court creed drawing on several faiths, centred on loyalty to himself.

beats.title: Jahangir Takes the Throne
beats.description: Akbar's son succeeded him at Agra and soon hung a chain of justice outside his palace for any subject to ring.

beats.title: Jahangir Marries Nur Jahan
beats.description: The emperor wed a widowed Persian noblewoman who would become the most powerful woman at the Mughal court.

beats.title: Thomas Roe Reaches Jahangir's Court
beats.description: An English ambassador sent by King James spent years at the emperor's court seeking trading rights for merchants.
beats.note: Roe presented credentials in 1616 in some accounts; arrival at Surat/Ajmer is 1615.

beats.title: Shah Jahan Ascends the Throne
beats.description: After a succession struggle among Jahangir's sons, a prince took the title King of the World and the Mughals' richest age began.

beats.title: Shah Jahan Begins the Taj Mahal
beats.description: An emperor started a white marble mausoleum at Agra for his beloved late wife, a project that took two decades.

beats.title: The Peacock Throne Is Unveiled
beats.description: A jewel-covered golden seat, set with a famous diamond and rubies, was completed after years of work for the emperor.

beats.title: Shah Jahan Begins the Red Fort
beats.description: The emperor laid the foundations of a vast red sandstone palace-fortress in a new walled capital on the Yamuna.

beats.title: Shah Jahan Begins the Jama Masjid
beats.description: Thousands of workers began India's largest mosque opposite the new palace, finished in about six years.

beats.title: Aurangzeb Seizes the Throne
beats.description: A prince defeated his brothers and imprisoned his ailing father in the fort at Agra, then had himself crowned emperor.

beats.title: Badshahi Mosque Is Completed
beats.description: A giant red sandstone mosque with marble domes opened at Lahore, among the largest in the world for centuries.

beats.title: Aurangzeb Reimposes the Jizya
beats.description: The emperor revived the tax on non-Muslims that his great-grandfather had abolished, stirring revolt among Hindu subjects.

beats.title: Aurangzeb Dies in the Deccan
beats.description: After decades of war in southern India the aging emperor died, and his sons fought over an empire starting to fray.

beats.title: Nadir Shah Sacks Delhi
beats.description: A Persian conqueror defeated the Mughal emperor at Karnal and carried off the Peacock Throne and the Koh-i-Noor diamond.

beats.title: Shah Alam II Returns to Delhi
beats.description: Escorted by Maratha troops, a Mughal emperor who had lived for years in exile re-entered his old capital as a figurehead.

beats.title: Bahadur Shah Zafar Becomes Emperor
beats.description: A poet-king inherited the Mughal title, with real power limited to the walls of his palace in Delhi.
beats.why_in: accession of the last Mughal emperor

beats.title: Last Mughal Emperor Is Deposed
beats.description: After joining a great uprising, the elderly emperor was captured, tried and sent into exile, ending the dynasty.
beats.note: Captured 1857, trial and exile to Rangoon 1858; used 1857.
